transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep noticing this rough, kind of sunken-looking patch on my face. In photos, or when I look in the mirror, it feels like one side of me looks old and beat-up. People tell me they can barely see anything, but I can’t really stop seeing it.

Does this concern about the appearance of that patch on your face cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, such as avoiding social situations or spending a lot of time checking it?

Yeah… I guess it does. I’ve been late getting out the door for jobs because I keep checking it. And I’ve been avoiding site photos… skipped a few family game nights too. Just don’t want people staring at my face.
Is your concern mainly about that patch on your face, or do you also worry about other areas or features of your body or face?

Mostly that patch on my face. I mean… that’s what I can’t stop seeing, especially in photos or the mirror. It just looks rough and kind of sunken to me, like one side of my face looks older or beat-up, even if people say they barely notice it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to try to fix or hide that patch on your face, like applying makeup, checking the mirror, or touching it?

Yeah… I do. Before work, or if I’m supposed to go to my sister’s game night, I’ll check it in the bathroom mirror a bunch. Turn my face different ways, different light. Sometimes I rub at it, like that’ll help. And if it looks bad to me, I’ll wear my hat low… or just make up a reason not to go.
Do you believe that the patch on your face looks much worse than others perceive it to be, or do you think others notice it as much as you do?

I guess… yeah, I think I see it a lot worse than other people do. They say they barely notice anything, but when I look in the mirror or see a photo, that rough, sunken patch is all I can see. Makes one side of my face look old and beat-up to me.

Yeah… it’s mostly that. I’m here because I just can’t stop seeing this rough, kind of sunken patch on my face. In photos or the mirror it jumps out at me, like one side of my face looks old or beat-up… even though people keep saying they barely notice anything.
Would you say that the patch you’re concerned about is something others can clearly see and comment on, or do they hardly notice it even when you point it out?

They hardly notice it, even when I point it out. They’ll say it’s not really anything… but I can’t stop seeing it in the mirror or in photos. It looks rough and kind of sunken to me, like that side of my face is worn out.
